name: Yandex Disk Sync

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
The progress notice appeared on every sync. Most syncs carry a single edited note and are over in a couple of seconds, so what should have been a background task kept interrupting instead.

## Show sync progress

A new setting, with three choices:

- **Only for long syncs** (default) — the indicator appears once a sync has been running for 20 seconds. Short ones come and go in silence; a long one still shows that something is happening.
- **Always** — the previous behaviour.
- **Never** — stays hidden regardless.

Asking for the indicator overrides the setting in every mode: tap the sync icon while a sync is running, or use the **Show sync status** command. "Never" does not mean unreachable.

When it does appear late, it opens showing the current state rather than the text it would have had twenty seconds earlier.

## Successful automatic syncs stay quiet

The result notice was the same interruption by another route: with a short poll interval it fired every time a note was edited. An automatic sync that went fine now says nothing.

Errors, files held back from being overwritten, and cancellations are still reported. A sync you start yourself always answers, including when there was nothing to do.
releases.name: 1.5.0 — the progress popup stops interrupting

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
Uploads and downloads shared a phase, so a note written on your device took its place in line among however many files the remote was sending. During a first sync of ~18,500 files that means it reaches the server hours later — and since the plugin runs one sync at a time, nothing else can carry it in the meantime.

Uploads are now a separate phase and run first. What you wrote here exists nowhere else yet; pulling the archive is catching up on data that is already safe.

Progress is also counted within each phase rather than across the whole run, so you see `Uploading 1/2` and then `Downloading 601/18562` instead of one opaque running total.

Requires [1.4.0](https://github.com/Nikolay-Eltsov/obsidian-yadisk-sync/releases/tag/1.4.0), which stopped edits made during a sync from being dropped altogether.
releases.name: 1.4.1 — your own edits are sent first

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
If you edited a note while a sync was running, the change stayed on disk but never reached Yandex Disk. This release fixes that, and closes a related window where such an edit could be overwritten outright.

## Edits during a sync

The vault event handler ignored everything while a sync was in progress. That guard was there to stop downloaded files from re-triggering a sync in a loop, but it could not tell the plugin's own writes from yours — so it swallowed both. The sync now reports each path it writes, and only those are ignored. A real edit schedules a sync as usual, and waits for the running one to finish instead of being dropped.

The auto-sync tick could not rescue it either. It decides whether to run by reading the disk revision, which never moves for a change made locally, so it always concluded nothing had happened. A pending local edit now forces a run regardless.

## Downloads no longer overwrite what you just typed

The transfer plan is built from a snapshot taken when the sync starts, which on a large vault is minutes before a given file is reached. A queued download could therefore land on top of a note edited while it waited.

Downloads now check that the local file is untouched, both before and after the transfer, and are abandoned if it moved. Those are reported as `kept:N`, and the next sync treats the file as the genuine two-sided conflict it is, resolving it under your chosen strategy.

## Getting the progress indicator back

A notice closes on any tap, and on mobile it is the only progress there is. Tapping the ribbon icon during a sync now re-shows it, and there is a **Show sync status** command.

---

First release built and signed by CI. Verify with:

```
gh attestation verify main.js --repo Nikolay-Eltsov/obsidian-yadisk-sync
```
releases.name: 1.4.0 — edits made during a sync are no longer lost

releases.author: Nikolay-Eltsov
releases.description:
Follow-up to [1.3.1](https://github.com/Nikolay-Eltsov/obsidian-yadisk-sync/releases/tag/1.3.1), addressing findings from the plugin review.

- **`authorUrl` was a dead link.** It pointed at `github.com/eltsov_ni`, which does not exist; the account is `Nikolay-Eltsov`. This link is shown in the community plugin listing.
- **Timers were scheduled on `activeWindow`**, which resolves to whichever window currently has focus. A debounce armed while a pop-out window was focused would never fire once that window closed, silently dropping the sync it had scheduled. All timers now use `window`.
- Removed the deprecated `autoSyncInterval` field from the settings type. It is only read as raw persisted data when migrating a pre-1.2 configuration, and is now stripped from what gets written back.
- Removed redundant `as unknown` casts.

No behavioural changes to sync itself.
releases.name: 1.3.2 — plugin review fixes

releases.author: Nikolay-Eltsov
releases.description:
Large vaults could not be synced from a phone. On a vault of ~12,000 files, tapping sync showed nothing at all and never finished. This release is mostly about that.

Two things were wrong. All progress went to the status bar, which does not exist on mobile, so the only feedback was a notice at the very end — and the "nothing to do" case didn't even show that. And transfers ran strictly one at a time, at two round trips per file: hours of work, none of which survived the app being backgrounded, because state was only saved once the whole run completed.

## Progress and control

- A progress indicator that works on mobile, with a **Cancel** button. It reports each phase with a live counter: scanning the vault, walking Yandex Disk, transferring.
- The result is always reported now, including when nothing needed syncing.
- Tapping sync while a sync is running says so instead of doing nothing silently.
- The conflict dialog no longer tries to render thousands of entries. It shows the first 200 and offers bulk actions for the rest.

## Speed

- **Parallel transfers**, configurable from 1 to 8 (default 4). This is where most of the gain is: on a 12,000-file tree at 300 ms latency, a first sync goes from roughly two hours to about half an hour, and to about fifteen minutes at the highest setting.
- Directory listings run concurrently, request only the fields the plugin reads, and use a page size of 1000 instead of 20.
- The redundant second full scan at the end of every sync is gone — executed actions are folded back into the snapshot instead.
- Uploading no longer probes every folder in a file's path. Known folders are remembered, and concurrent uploads into the same new folder create it once.

## Auto-sync

- The interval is now chosen from a list starting at **every 10 seconds**, rather than typed in whole minutes. An existing setting is migrated.
- A poll costs a single request. Yandex Disk exposes a counter that changes when anything on the account changes; if it hasn't moved, the plugin does nothing — no scan, no UI.
- The same check means a sync caused by editing a note skips the remote walk entirely. Edit a file on your phone and it reaches the server in about five seconds, regardless of vault size.
- Automatic syncs stay quiet unless they actually moved something.

## Interrupted syncs

- State is checkpointed every 15 seconds, so a sync that is cancelled or cut short resumes instead of restarting. Previously nothing was saved until the very end.
- Snapshots are stored more compactly.
- On returning to Obsidian after switching away, a sync starts immediately rather than waiting out another interval.
- **Keep screen on during long syncs** (new setting, on by default) stops the screen lock from suspending the app halfway through a large transfer on iOS.

## Fixes

- Network failures were never retried. The retry only matched `TypeError`, which `requestUrl` does not throw, so a single blip anywhere in a long sync aborted the whole thing.
- A `429` now pauses every transfer and honours `Retry-After`, rather than each request backing off alone while the others keep pushing.
- Directory pagination could loop forever if the API reported a file count inconsistent with what it returned, which looked exactly like a hang.
- Pagination no longer assumes the server honoured the requested page size, which could silently skip the rest of a large folder.
- **Push all** and **Pull all** now transfer a file that exists on one side only, even when an earlier run had already recorded it. Such a file was previously never sent, in either direction.
- Editing settings no longer rewrites the entire sync state on every keystroke.

## Note on requirements

`minAppVersion` is now **1.6.6**, which is what the plugin has actually required since it began using `fileManager.trashFile`. Earlier releases claimed 0.15.0 incorrectly.
releases.name: 1.3.1 — large vaults on mobile

releases.author: Nikolay-Eltsov
releases.description:
## Bug fix

Fixed a critical sync error: Yandex Disk API returns resource paths prefixed with `disk:` (e.g. `disk:/ObsidianVault/file.md`), but `toLocalPath` was not stripping this prefix. As a result, the full `disk:/...` path leaked into the sync plan, and on download `toRemotePath` produced a malformed path like `/ObsidianVault/disk:/ObsidianVault/file.md`, causing a `400 DiskAreaDoesNotExistsError` from the API.

**If you ran 1.1.2 and got 400 errors:** go to plugin settings → **Reset sync state**, then run sync again.

releases.author: Nikolay-Eltsov
releases.description:
## Bug fix

Files were silently skipped during sync after a previously failed download. When a download failed, the remote snapshot was saved recording those files as known, but since they never appeared locally, the sync engine had no matching branch in its decision logic and fell through to Skip on every subsequent run.

**Fix:** added explicit rules in `decideSyncAction` — if a file exists on one side but was never tracked on the other, treat it as new and sync it.

**If your vault is stuck showing "Synced" with no files downloaded:** go to plugin settings → **Reset sync state**, then run sync again.

releases.author: Nikolay-Eltsov
releases.description:
## Bug fix

Restore `vault.createFolder` instead of `vault.adapter.mkdir` for creating local folders during download. The adapter method creates the folder only on disk without updating Obsidian's in-memory file tree, causing file creation to fail.

releases.author: Nikolay-Eltsov
releases.description:
## What's changed

- Fix plugin review warnings:
  - `createEl("div")` → `createDiv()` in conflict modal
  - `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` → `activeWindow` variants for popout window compatibility
  - `resp.json as Type` → `resp.json as unknown as Type` to satisfy strict any-safety rules
  - `ButtonComponent.setDisabled` → `buttonEl.disabled` (compatible with minAppVersion 0.15.0)
  - `Vault.createFolder` → `vault.adapter.mkdir` (compatible with minAppVersion 0.15.0)
